person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the word `prebiotic` - what it has meant since 1995, what it should mean now, and which substances fall inside and outside the category
span.quote: Consistent with the original embodiment of prebiotics, but aware of the latest scientific and clinical developments, the panel updated the definition of a prebiotic: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit. This definition expands the concept of prebiotics to possibly include non-carbohydrate substances, applications to body sites other than the gastrointestinal tract, and diverse categories other than food. The requirement for selective microbiota-mediated mechanisms was retained. Beneficial health effects must be documented for a substance to be considered a prebiotic.

span.label: whether the 1995 definition still fits the evidence, and specifically whether selectivity, the colon and the food category should remain part of what the term requires
span.quote: Consistent with the original embodiment of prebiotics, but aware of the latest scientific and clinical developments, the panel updated the definition of a prebiotic: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit. span.label: a consensus definition - a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit - which restores the selectivity requirement a 2010 definition had removed, drops the restriction to the gut and to food, and names what is excluded

span.label: method
span.quote: To prepare, panellists developed a discussion outline and target questions. Several delivered brief presentations that addressed background and core issues. Discussion ensued for each issue until consensus was achieved. After the meeting, individual panellists wrote sections of the summary, which were compiled by G.R.G., M.E.S and G.R. into a draft report. This docu­ ment was edited and agreed upon by all panel members, and finally by the ISAPP board of directors.

span.label: a scientific category being fixed by deliberation rather than discovered - twelve named experts, one day, a printed history of the previous definitions and a figure with a NOT PREBIOTIC column
span.quote: Ultimately, the goal of this Consensus Statement is to engender appropriate use of the term ‘prebiotic’ by relevant stakeholders so that consistency and clarity can be achieved in research reports, product marketing and regulatory oversight of the category.

span.label: an expert panel convened by ISAPP: discussion outline and target questions, presentations, discussion per issue until consensus, sections written by individual panellists, compiled, edited and agreed by all members and the board
span.term: an expert panel convened by ISAPP: discussion outline and target questions, presentations, discussion per issue until consensus, sections written by individual panellists, compiled, edited and agreed by all members and the board
span.quote: To prepare, panellists developed a discussion outline and target questions. Several delivered brief presentations that addressed background and core issues. This docu­ ment was edited and agreed upon by all panel members, and finally by the ISAPP board of directors.

span.label: the panel prints the 1995 wording, the three criteria it implied, the 2010 revision that removed selective fermentation and confined prebiotics to the gut, and then its own. A reader can see which requirement was dropped and put back, which is the record most redefinitions do not leave
span.term: a definition with a history attached
span.quote: This definition limited pre­ biotics to interactions with the gut microbiota (excluding extraintestinal sites such as vagina and skin) and removed the requirement for selective fermentation. Selectivity with respect to microbial fermentation is viewed by this panel as key to the prebiotic concept.

span.label: antibiotics, minerals, vitamins and bacteriophages are named as NOT prebiotics even though they alter the microbiota. Defining by exclusion tests the criterion where it is hardest - on things that produce the same observable effect by a different mechanism
span.quote: Substrates that affect composition of the microbiota through mechanisms not involving selective utilization by host microorganisms are not prebiotics. These sub­ strates would include antibiotics, minerals, vitamins and bacteriophages, which are not growth substrates, even though their intake might alter microbiota and metabolic composition.

span.label: butyrate generated by pathogens with a bad outcome for the host is not a prebiotic effect. So membership depends jointly on the substrate, on which organisms used it and on what happened to the host - and none of that is measurable from the substance alone
span.term: the category is a property of the event, not the substance
span.quote: However, if pathogenic microorganisms are involved in butyrate generation and a negative consequence occurs for the host, then it cannot be termed a prebiotic. This distinction makes it important to determine both function and composition of the gut microbiota involved.

span.label: the panel requires assessment of the full microbial diversity in vivo and calls inference from pure or co-culture inadequate. Widening a category while raising its evidence bar is what stops a broader definition from admitting more claims
span.term: the evidence standard raised at the same time as the definition
span.quote: Making inferences on prebiotic effects from pure or co­culture experiments is inadequate. Similarly, any conclusion regarding prebiotic activity must be based on an assessment of the full microbial diversity, not simply increased abundance of gut bifido bacteria or lacto bacilli, for example.

span.label: ISAPP raises funds through an Industry Advisory Committee, and the statement records that no input into this consensus process came from its members. The disclosure is placed in the methods, next to the procedure it could have influenced
span.term: the conflict declared where it would operate
span.quote: Through its Industry Advisory Committee, ISAPP incorporates indus­ try scien tists in its activities and raises funds to advance its mission. However, no input into this consensus panel process was provided by members of the Industry Advisory Committee.

span.label: A DEFINITION FAILED BY ITS EXTENSION AND THE PAPER SAYS SO: the 2008 FAO/UN wording dropped selective fermentation, and `IN DOING SO THE DEFINITION WAS CRITICIZED FOR NOT EXCLUDING ANTIBIOTICS`. An intergovernmental panel widened a category until it admitted the one class of substance the category exists to be distinguished from - and the corpus already carries `antibiotics` on this record as the named excluded case.
span.quote: The Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO) of the United Nations (UN) organized a Technical Meeting to update the defin­ ition of prebiotics in 2008. This panel proposed that prebiotics be redefined as “a non­viable food component that confers a health benefit on the host associated with modulation of the microbiota” (REF. 19). Here, selective fermentation was removed as a criterion, but in doing so the definition was criticized for not excluding anti­ biotics

span.label: THE REPAIR WAS A NEW NAME, NOT AN AMENDMENT: two years after the 2008 wording failed, `Gibson et al.20 ... defined the NARROWER CATEGORY of ‘dietary prebiotics’ as “a SELECTIVELY FERMENTED ingredient”`. Rather than revise the term that had gone wrong, the field minted a second term carrying the criterion the first had lost - and then in 2015 the unqualified term moved AGAIN, the other way.
span.quote: Gibson et al.20, 2 years later, defined the narrower category of ‘dietary prebiotics’ as “a selectively fermented ingredient that results in specific changes in the compo­ sition and/or activity of the gastrointestinal microbiota, thus conferring benefit(s) upon host health

span.label: AND THE PANEL RECORDS WHY IT PICKED ONE WORD: `The term ‘substrate’ was chosen for its meaning of a substance on or from which an organism obtains its nourishment`. A consensus body justifying a single lexical choice in print, in a box headed as justification for the new definition.
span.quote: The term ‘substrate’ was chosen for its meaning of a substance on or from which an organism obtains its nourishment

span.label: THE STATED TRIGGER FOR A CONSENSUS IS THE PLURALITY OF DEFINITIONS ITSELF: `GIVEN THE PROPOSED DEFINITIONS ALREADY DESCRIBED, AS WELL AS OTHERS, THE NEED FOR A CONSENSUS DEFINITION WAS EVIDENT`. The paper treats the count of competing definitions as sufficient grounds to convene a panel - and says `as well as others`, so the five it prints are not the whole set.
span.quote: Given the proposed definitions already described, as well as others, the need for a consensus definition was evi­ dent23. This need was amplified by views that the pre biotic concept required clarification on specificity, mech anisms of effect, health attributes and relevance

span.label: currently established prebiotics are carbohydrate-based, and non-carbohydrate candidates only might fit the updated definition pending convincing evidence
span.quote: Currently established prebiotics are carbohydrate-based, but other substances such as polyphenols and polyunsaturated fatty acids converted to respective conjugated fatty acids might fit the updated definition assuming convincing weight of evidence in the target host • The beneficial effect(s) of a prebiotic on health must be confirmed in the target animal for its intended use and mediated through the microbiota

span.label: the health benefit must be documented for a substance to be considered a prebiotic, so the category cannot be assigned from chemistry alone
span.quote: Consistent with the original embodiment of prebiotics, but aware of the latest scientific and clinical developments, the panel updated the definition of a prebiotic: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit. This definition expands the concept of prebiotics to possibly include non-carbohydrate substances, applications to body sites other than the gastrointestinal tract, and diverse categories other than food. The requirement for selective microbiota-mediated mechanisms was retained. Beneficial health effects must be documented for a substance to be considered a prebiotic.

span.label: inference about prebiotic effects from pure or co-culture experiments is inadequate; conclusions require the full microbiota in vivo
span.quote: Making inferences on prebiotic effects from pure or co­culture experiments is inadequate. Similarly, any conclusion regarding prebiotic activity must be based on an assessment of the full microbial diversity, not simply increased abundance of gut bifido bacteria or lacto bacilli, for example.

span.label: prebiotic
span.quote: Consistent with the original embodiment of prebiotics, but aware of the latest scientific and clinical developments, the panel updated the definition of a prebiotic: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit. This definition expands the concept of prebiotics to possibly include non-carbohydrate substances, applications to body sites other than the gastrointestinal tract, and diverse categories other than food. The requirement for selective microbiota-mediated mechanisms was retained. Beneficial health effects must be documented for a substance to be considered a prebiotic.

span.label: probiotics
span.quote: Whereas probiotics use live microorganisms, prebiotics are non­viable substrates that serve as nutrients for beneficial microorganisms harboured by the host, including administered pro biotic strains and indigenous (resident) microorganisms. Thus, prebiotics differ from most dietary fibres such as pectins, cellulose and xylans, which encourage growth of a wide variety of gut microorganisms. Our meaning here is that a prebiotic should not be broadly metabolized, but elicit a metabolism biased towards health­promoting microorganisms within the indigenous ecosystem.

span.label: prebiotic - AS DEFINED IN 1995: a non-digestible FOOD ingredient that selectively stimulates one or a limited number of bacteria ALREADY RESIDENT IN THE COLON
span.quote: Although dietary oligosaccharides had long been used to impart health benefits, principally in Asia, the prebiotic concept was first defined in 1995 as a “non­ digestible food ingredient that beneficially affects the host by selectively stimulating the growth and/or activity of one or a limited number of bacteria already resident in the colon” (REF. 4).

span.label: prebiotic - AS DEFINED IN 2015 by Bindels et al.: limited to the gut microbiota, excluding extraintestinal sites such as vagina and skin, and with the requirement for selective fermentation REMOVED - the definition this panel was convened to replace
span.quote: This definition limited pre­ biotics to interactions with the gut microbiota (excluding extraintestinal sites such as vagina and skin) and removed the requirement for selective fermentation. Selectivity with respect to microbial fermentation is viewed by this panel as key to the prebiotic concept.

span.label: prebiotic - AS DEFINED IN 2017: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit - selectivity restored, no food requirement, no site requirement
span.quote: now proposes the following definition of a pre biotic: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host micro­ organisms conferring a health benefit (BOX 1). See BOX 2 for additional rationale used to adopt this new definition.

span.label: prebiotic - BY WHAT IT EXCLUDES: not antibiotics, minerals, vitamins or bacteriophages, which alter the microbiota without being growth substrates
span.quote: Substrates that affect composition of the microbiota through mechanisms not involving selective utilization by host microorganisms are not prebiotics. These sub­ strates would include antibiotics, minerals, vitamins and bacteriophages, which are not growth substrates, even though their intake might alter microbiota and metabolic composition.

span.label: a prebiotic effect - AS A PROPERTY OF THE SUBSTANCE: what the category name suggests, and what the panel rejects
span.quote: However, if pathogenic microorganisms are involved in butyrate generation and a negative consequence occurs for the host, then it cannot be termed a prebiotic. This distinction makes it important to determine both function and composition of the gut microbiota involved.

span.label: a prebiotic effect - AS A PROPERTY OF THE WHOLE EVENT: if pathogens generate the butyrate and the host is harmed, the same molecule is not a prebiotic effect
span.quote: However, if pathogenic microorganisms are involved in butyrate generation and a negative consequence occurs for the host, then it cannot be termed a prebiotic. This distinction makes it important to determine both function and composition of the gut microbiota involved.

span.label: evidence of prebiotic activity - AS PRACTISED: increased abundance of bifidobacteria or lactobacilli
span.quote: Making inferences on prebiotic effects from pure or co­culture experiments is inadequate. Similarly, any conclusion regarding prebiotic activity must be based on an assessment of the full microbial diversity, not simply increased abundance of gut bifido bacteria or lacto bacilli, for example.

span.label: evidence of prebiotic activity - AS REQUIRED HERE: an assessment of the full microbial diversity in vivo, with pure and co-culture inference called inadequate
span.quote: Making inferences on prebiotic effects from pure or co­culture experiments is inadequate. Similarly, any conclusion regarding prebiotic activity must be based on an assessment of the full microbial diversity, not simply increased abundance of gut bifido bacteria or lacto bacilli, for example.

span.label: prebiotic - AS DEFINED IN 2004: `selectively fermented ingredients that allow specific changes ... in the gastrointestinal microflora that confers benefits upon host well-being and health`, carrying THREE explicit criteria - resist host digestion, be fermented by intestinal microorganisms, and selectively stimulate health-associated intestinal bacteria.
span.quote: In 2004, the definition of pre biotics was altered to “selectively fer­ mented ingredients that allow specific changes, both in the composition and/or activity in the gastrointestinal microflora that confers benefits upon host well­being and health” (REF. 18). As per this definition, three criteria were required for a prebiotic: the ability to resist host digestion (for example gastric acidity, hydrolysis by mammalian enzymes and gastrointestinal absorption); that they are fermented by intestinal microorganisms; and that they selectively stimulate the growth and/or activity of intestinal bac teria associated with health and well­being

span.label: prebiotic - AS DEFINED IN 2008 BY AN FAO/UN TECHNICAL MEETING: `a non-viable food component that confers a health benefit on the host associated with modulation of the microbiota`. SELECTIVE FERMENTATION WAS REMOVED, AND THE DEFINITION WAS THEN CRITICISED FOR NOT EXCLUDING ANTIBIOTICS - a definition whose extension was wrong in a way anyone could check.
span.quote: The Food and Agricultural Organization (FAO) of the United Nations (UN) organized a Technical Meeting to update the defin­ ition of prebiotics in 2008. This panel proposed that prebiotics be redefined as “a non­viable food component that confers a health benefit on the host associated with modulation of the microbiota” (REF. 19). Here, selective fermentation was removed as a criterion, but in doing so the definition was criticized for not excluding anti­ biotics

span.label: dietary prebiotics - A NARROWER SIBLING TERM COINED IN 2010 TO REPAIR THE 2008 DEFINITION: `a selectively fermented ingredient that results in specific changes in the composition and/or activity of the gastrointestinal microbiota`. The repair was made by NAMING A NEW TERM rather than by amending the old one, and it RESTORED the criterion 2008 had dropped.

span.quote: Ultimately, the goal of this Consensus Statement is to engender appropriate use of the term ‘prebiotic’ by relevant stakeholders so that consistency and clarity can be achieved in research reports, product marketing and regulatory oversight of the category.

span.label: 2017 ISAPP: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit - expanded to non-carbohydrates, to sites beyond the gut and to categories beyond food, with the selectivity requirement retained
span.quote: now proposes the following definition of a pre biotic: a substrate that is selectively utilized by host micro­ organisms conferring a health benefit (BOX 1). See BOX 2 for additional rationale used to adopt this new definition. Prebiotic effect and selectivity Prebiotics are not the only substances that can affect the microbiota10 (FIG. 1)

span.label: 1995: a non-digestible food ingredient that beneficially affects the host by selectively stimulating the growth and/or activity of one or a limited number of bacteria already resident in the colon
span.quote: Although dietary oligosaccharides had long been used to impart health benefits, principally in Asia, the prebiotic concept was first defined in 1995 as a “non­ digestible food ingredient that beneficially affects the host by selectively stimulating the growth and/or activity of one or a limited number of bacteria already resident in the colon” (REF. 4).

span.label: selective utilization
span.quote: Substrates that affect composition of the microbiota through mechanisms not involving selective utilization by host microorganisms are not prebiotics. These sub­ strates would include antibiotics, minerals, vitamins and bacteriophages, which are not growth substrates, even though their intake might alter microbiota and metabolic composition.
